o1.biggest_strength: Every concept is anchored to a number in my data (70% of spend on men, women at ₹1,058, 290 quiet-wheel mentions, 85 scuff reviews) and the launch plan tells me what to run first, on what budget (3x ₹1,515) and what to judge.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some concepts stay thin on production detail (no aspect-ratio/safe-zone or headline specs for the designer), and the per-trip maths quietly treats two flights a month as 24 trips, which a careful reader may query.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a designer-ready shot list and on-screen copy limits per concept, plus a clear kill/scale rule, so nothing comes back to me as homework.

o2.biggest_strength: The build rules make it hand-off ready: aspect ratios, safe zones, headline character counts (all counted correctly), no front pocket, lighter shells for the scuff issue.
o2.biggest_mistake: The primary texts repeat '₹6,999' and a spec list in almost every ad, so the copy reads like a product sheet rather than our calm voice, and two of the top three put money back into the expensive men's audience when women are the cheaper win.

reason: Both read my numbers correctly, but Output 1's copy I could paste tomorrow in our voice and its first three put the cheap women's audience where the data says it belongs, while Output 2 buys production polish at the cost of brand voice and doubles down on men.
